title: Redwood POC scoping with HorizonCare - security pilot
summary: Initial POC scoping focused on security/compliance needs for a HorizonCare pilot. Discussed SOC 2 and ISO documents, SSO/SAML SSO flow, role-based access controls, audit log retention (1 year+), KMS/HSM integration, need for BAA for PHI, benchmark plans (latency/throughput/quality), workload sizing and a ~6 week pilot timeline with defined success criteria and next steps.
transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2028-10-19
- Time: 16:00 PT
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Alicia Monroe (CISO, HorizonCare), Dr. Rajiv Kapoor (Head of AI), Maya Lin (PM), Evan Torres (Platform Eng), Lisa Chen (Legal)

[00:00] Jordan Blake: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood, joined by samira our solutions engineer, quick agenda — scope the poc security requirements, dimensions for benchmarks, and timelines. 
[00:12] Alicia Monroe: thanks, jordan. big picture is we want to validate both performance and that redwood meets our security bar before we do anything with PHI. SOC 2 and ISO are mandatory, and we need a BAA for the pilot if any patient data is involved.
[00:28] Samira Patel: yep totally understood; we typically run a security pilot where we provide SOC 2 attestations and ISO27001 summary, and for PHI we require an executed BAA. we'll also run the benchmark on isolated test data unless you want us to use a de-id set.
[00:42] Dr. Rajiv Kapoor: a de-identified set is fine for initial perf and quality tests. later we may want to run on a small slice of real records under BAA. what are typical throughput numbers we can expect for a dedicated pilot?
[00:55] Samira Patel: for dedicated capacity with a medium model and 512 token contexts you can expect roughly X throughput — sorry those numbers vary by model; for sizing the pilot let's align on expected concurrency and tokens per request. what does horizoncare expect?
[01:10] Evan Torres: we're thinking about a front-door clinical summarization flow, roughly 50 concurrent users at peak, avg 200 tokens per request, maybe 5k requests per day. latency target is p95 < 1.2s ideally.
[01:24] Jordan Blake: that seems reasonable for a pilot — we can provision dedicated capacity and run a 2-week benchmark to validate p50/p95 latency and cost. success criteria could be: p95 latency below 1.2s for 200-token prompts, throughput of 5k req/day without queuing, plus quality thresholds on your evaluation prompts.
[01:42] Maya Lin: quality thresholds — we need a clear metric. we'll provide a prompt set of 200 examples and our scoring rubric. we want automated evals and regression checks between model variants.
[01:53] Samira Patel: we can run evals and provide the regression dashboard; we also include token-level cost breakdowns in the console.
[02:03] Lisa Chen: from legal, we need to make sure audit logs show who accessed what and when, with retention at least 12 months. also need SSO integrations for SAML SSO and scoping for RBAC so we can separate clinical, research, and infra roles.
[02:20] Jordan Blake: absolutely — our private deployment supports SAML SSO and SSO federation; we also have RBAC with role templates (admin, developer, viewer) and can extend for clinical roles. audit logs are captured at the token/request level and are exportable — retention default is 90 days on hosted but for Dedicated/Private we can support 12 months or longer per contract.
[02:42] Alicia Monroe: good. KMS — can you integrate with our AWS KMS or HSM for key management? we need customer-managed keys and encryption at rest and in transit.
[02:53] Samira Patel: yes, we support AWS KMS and Vault/HSM integrations for private installs; for hosted we offer envelope encryption and will support CMKs for Dedicated/Private deployments. we'll note that in the security pack.
[03:06] Dr. Rajiv Kapoor: penetration testing — do you perform pen tests and share reports? we need to know scope, cadence, and whether redwood will coordinate or we do our own against a staging environment.
[03:18] Jordan Blake: redwood does internal pen tests and we've contracted third-party assessments; we can share summary reports and coordinate a customer-led scoping test on a dedicated pilot environment under NDA.
[03:31] Evan Torres: network isolation — for the pilot we want VPC peering or private connectivity. can we get a VPC/private deployment for the POC?
[03:41] Samira Patel: for pilots we can do a private deployment in your VPC or a customer-managed private control plane. tradeoff is setup time — a private pilot usually adds ~2 weeks to provisioning.
[03:52] Jordan Blake: timeline suggestion: week 0 — contract + BAA + security paperwork; week 1 — provision dedicated/private pilot environment and SAML SSO integration; week 2 — run baseline benchmarks and evals; week 3 — tune and run second-round benchmarks; week 4 — finalize results and decision. overall ~4-6 weeks.
[04:12] Alicia Monroe: that timeline is tight but workable. we need the SOC2/ISO docs up-front; can you send the security pack and your SOC 2 report?
[04:21] Jordan Blake: yes — action: samira will send SOC 2 attestation, ISO summary, network diagrams, and our standard BAA template.
[04:29] Lisa Chen: we'll want to review the BAA and potentially redline. also please include interface for audit log exports and retention SLAs in the doc.
[04:38] Samira Patel: noted. regarding SAML, do you use Okta? Azure AD?
[04:43] Alicia Monroe: we're on Okta.
[04:45] Samira Patel: great — we have an Okta SAML integration guide; we can pre-configure a test app for the pilot.
[04:52] Dr. Rajiv Kapoor: on data handling — for de-id we will provide a synthetic/de-identified set for initial quality tests; if results look good we'll plan a small PHI test under BAA. need to confirm data deletion/retention policies after the pilot.
[05:05] Jordan Blake: standard pilot policy: for Dedicated/Private we can guarantee no customer data is used for model training and logs are retained per contract and deletable on request; we'll include data deletion procedures in the security pack.
[05:18] Evan Torres: one more — RBAC mapping: can we sync groups from Okta to roles in Redwood? we need group-based access so clinicians only see clinical routes and research gets broader eval access.
[05:30] Samira Patel: yes, group mapping from IdP to RBAC roles is supported; we'll include an example mapping doc.
[05:38] Maya Lin: final question — what does the benchmark harness look like? can we run it remotely or do you need us to run scripts in our env?
[05:46] Samira Patel: we provide a benchmark harness that can run from our environment hitting the pilot cluster or you can run it inside your VPC and upload results. for apples-to-apples we'll run both sides if needed.
[06:00] Jordan Blake: ok let's recap and assign next steps.

Recap & Next Steps in conversation:
[06:10] Jordan Blake: 1) samira to send security pack (SOC 2, ISO, pen test summaries), BAA template, SAML/Okta guide, network diagram.
[06:20] Samira Patel: 2) horizoncare to provide de-identified prompt set (200 examples) and success rubric; indicate whether you want synthetic PHI later.
[06:30] Jordan Blake: 3) horizoncare infra to confirm expected concurrency and tokens per request (evan to confirm) so we size dedicated capacity.
[06:38] Evan Torres: will send numbers by monday.
[06:41] Lisa Chen: 4) legal will review BAA, aim to have comments within two weeks.
[06:48] Dr. Rajiv Kapoor: 5) plan for a 4-6 week pilot once paperwork is done.

[06:55] Jordan Blake: thanks everyone; we'll follow up with calendar invites for provisioning kickoff and share the docs.
[07:02] Alicia Monroe: thanks, talk soon.

Note: transcript includes some auto-caption artifacts; names occasionally garbled (e.g., 'samira' transcribed as 'sameera' in places).
